payload.chart:
The architecture is ruled, so this chart covers only the implementation choices the ruling leaves open. Rows are the decisions that actually remain; pruned cells carry their reason.

ROW 1 - how the events leave the merge's tree. (a) merge --no-commit, then drop the paths from index and worktree, then commit - PROBED WORKING (run-aa90b5a988e9). (b) build the tree by hand with read-tree/write-tree and commit-tree - pruned: strictly more machinery for the same result, and it fails criterion C5, ordinary mechanics. (c) merge everything then delete in a FOLLOW-UP commit - pruned: trunk would carry the events for one commit, so a checkout of that commit still contains them, and the invariant would be true only eventually. (d) merge -s ours then selectively check out claims - pruned: inverts the default, so any claim not explicitly listed is silently dropped; the failure mode is losing claims, which is worse than leaking events.

ROW 2 - how content is classified as claim or event. (a) path rules held by the engine (evidence/, machines/, state.json under an iteration's directory) - chosen: the layout already encodes the distinction, and the rule is inspectable in one place. (b) a frontmatter field on every node - pruned: evidence documents are JSON runs, not nodes with frontmatter, so it cannot cover the heavy material. (c) per-iteration configuration - pruned: makes the invariant negotiable per iteration, which is how a rule erodes.

ROW 3 - when the milestone commit fires. (a) on each gate bless - chosen: the bless window is already the sanctioned commit moment, so nothing new is invented. (b) on every loop submit - pruned: commits per step, far below milestone granularity, and it would bury the branch history. (c) on a timer - pruned: commits unrelated to any process boundary.

ROW 4 - where the tag is created. (a) before the merge, at close - chosen: risk R1 requires the record be named before it leaves the tree. (b) after a successful merge - pruned: leaves a window where events are out of the tree and unnamed. (c) at open - pruned: the tag would point at an empty branch and need moving, and moving a tag is the kind of history mutation R11 forbids in spirit.

ROW 5 - how a closed iteration stays listable. (a) from the grant index on trunk - chosen: it already names every iteration and stays on trunk by the owner's ruling. (b) a stub directory left behind per iteration - pruned: reintroduces exactly the clutter this iteration removes. (c) read it from git tags now - pruned: that is i5e, and doing it here breaks the binding excluded list.
payload.shortlist: One combination is seeded, and that is a deliberate strike rather than an oversight: 1a + 2a + 3a + 4a + 5a. Every alternative above was pruned on a stated failure, not on preference - three of them (1c, 1d, 4b) fail the veto criterion C1 or the invariant itself, and the rest fail C5 or the binding scope. Elaborating a second candidate would mean elaborating one already known to fail a veto criterion, which is decision theater by the design's own definition. Static partitioning for the seeded combination is the clustering already recorded: the milestone lane and the pointer ride the bless path, the atomic close rides shipMerge, the working place rides provisioning, and the erasure constraint sits over the git invocation layer. Feasibility is not rough - it is probed.
